questions.q: In `docker build -t my-ai-app:1.0 .`, what does the trailing `.` specify?
options: The build context — the directory Docker sends to the build, which is what COPY can see
questions.explain: The build context is sent to the Docker daemon so COPY . . has something to find; -t is what actually sets the tag.

questions.q: Which flag actually opens a port so traffic can reach the container, unlike the Dockerfile's EXPOSE?
questions.explain: EXPOSE in the Dockerfile only documents the port; -p at `docker run` is what publishes it to the host.

questions.q: What does `docker exec -it ai-app sh` let you do?
options: Open a shell inside an already-running container, to inspect it directly
questions.explain: docker exec runs a command inside a container that's already running — the fastest way to check what's actually there, without rebuilding anything.

questions.q: What does `CACHED` next to a build step in `docker build` output mean?
options: Docker reused a previous layer instead of re-running that instruction
That instruction failed and was skipped
Docker is downloading that layer from a registry
The image will be smaller than usual
questions.explain: It's the build cache from Lesson 3 in action — an unchanged instruction (and everything before it) gets served from cache instead of re-executed.

questions.q: Why would you add `--rm` to a `docker run` command?
options: To mount a host folder into the container
To automatically delete the container the moment it exits, for short, disposable runs
questions.explain: --rm is for runs you don't need to keep around afterward, like a one-off command to check a package version.
